chunks: ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the divorce of the mentally impaired one whose intellect has departed: is it valid? He said: “No.”
And about the woman, if she is in that same condition, is her sale and her charity valid? He said: “No.”

key_terms.الزَّائِلِ: one whose faculty has departed or diminished
key_terms.الْعَقْلِ: intellect or mental capacity required for legal validity
key_terms.الْمَعْتُوهِ: a mentally impaired person lacking full legal competence
key_terms.بَيْعُهَا: her sale, meaning her act of selling property
key_terms.صَدَقَتُهَا: her charity or charitable disposal of wealth
key_terms.طَلَاقِ: divorce as a legal act dissolving marriage

ai.seo_question: Is the divorce or financial transaction of a mentally impaired person valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that acts requiring legal capacity are not valid from a person whose intellect is impaired. It addresses both divorce and the financial disposal of property, indicating that such actions are not recognized when mental soundness is absent.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4770 - Abd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr narrated from al-Ḥalabi from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:

I asked Imam (as) about the divorce of a mentally impaired person whose intellect is diminished, whether it is permissible?
Imam (as) replied: "No."

I (narrator) also asked about a woman in the same condition, whether it is permissible to sell her property or manage her dowry?
He replied: "No."
